title: Basilicata's LPG Prices Have Gone Nowhere Since July — While Italy's Climbed Nearly 9% Around It
dek: The region's daily fuel snapshot for November 20 shows gasoline and diesel both easing for a second straight day, Metano holding at a tracked high, and GPL stuck near its lowest point of the season even as the national average pulls away.
executive_summary: As of November 20, 2026, self-service prices in Basilicata stood at €1.9888/L for Benzina, €2.2448/L for Gasolio, €0.799/L for GPL, and €2.199/L for Metano, with 238 of the region's 268 registered stations reporting that day. Benzina and Gasolio both eased slightly for a second straight day while GPL and Metano held flat — a quiet day on the surface, though Basilicata's GPL ran about 3.9% below the national self-service average while its Metano ran about 4.4% above it.

The real divergence shows up once you zoom out to the weekly data. Since Fuel Dashboard's tracking began on July 21, 2026, Italy's national GPL average has climbed 9.3%, while Basilicata's has actually fallen 1.8% over the same stretch — the two have been moving in opposite directions for months. Metano tells almost the reverse story: both region and country have risen sharply since July, but Basilicata's 57.1% increase has comfortably outpaced the 40.9% national rise, widening the region's premium over the Italian average even as both numbers plateaued through November.

fuel_sections.heading: Gasoline Keeps Easing, Now Within a Few Cents of Where It Started
paragraphs: Basilicata's self-service Benzina price was €1.9888/L on November 20, down €0.0019 (-0.10%) from €1.9907/L the day before — a second consecutive day of mild declines. That puts the region €0.0290/L above Italy's national self-service average of €1.9598/L, a premium of about 1.5%.

Zoomed out, Benzina in Basilicata rose from €1.9866/L in the week of July 20 to a tracked peak of €2.1796/L in the week of September 21, then rolled over, easing to €1.9935/L by the week of November 16 — down 8.5% from that peak but still +0.35% above where tracking began in July. Italy traced an almost identical arc, also peaking the week of September 21 (€2.1669/L) before falling to €1.9652/L, a slightly steeper 9.3% drop from its own peak that left the national average -0.5% below its July starting point. The upshot: both region and country rallied and retreated on nearly the same schedule, but Basilicata's round trip has left it fractionally ahead of where it started while Italy's has left it fractionally behind.

fuel_sections.heading: Diesel Cools From Its September High, Slower Than the National Pullback
paragraphs: Basilicata's self-service Gasolio price was €2.2448/L on November 20, down €0.0014 (-0.06%) from €2.2462/L the previous day. The region sits €0.0158/L above the €2.229/L national self-service average, a gap of about 0.7%.

On the weekly view, Gasolio in Basilicata rose from €2.1793/L (week of July 20) to a tracked peak of €2.3723/L in the week of September 21, then eased to €2.2489/L by the week of November 16 — a 5.2% retreat from the peak, leaving it +3.2% above its July starting level. Nationally, Gasolio peaked slightly higher at €2.3736/L the same week before falling to €2.2324/L, a steeper 6.0% drop from the high but a smaller net gain of +2.65% since July. Diesel's autumn comedown has therefore trimmed a bit more off the national average than off Basilicata's, so the region's cushion above its starting price has stayed a touch wider than Italy's.

fuel_sections.heading: LPG Diverges Sharply From a Rising National Trend
paragraphs: Basilicata's self-service GPL price held flat at €0.799/L on November 20, unchanged from the day before. That's €0.0323/L, or 3.9%, below the €0.8313/L national self-service average — the region's widest discount among the four fuels tracked today.

This is the day's standout divergence. Since the week of July 20, Basilicata's GPL has actually fallen 1.8% (from €0.814/L to €0.799/L), spending most of September and October at a tracked low of €0.7857/L before ticking up only slightly in early November. Over the same stretch, Italy's national GPL average has climbed 9.3% (from €0.7592/L to €0.8295/L), with most of that increase arriving since mid-October. The result is a fuel moving in opposite directions regionally and nationally: Basilicata's LPG has essentially flatlined-to-declined for four months while the rest of the country has paid steadily more for it.

fuel_sections.heading: Natural Gas Keeps Climbing Faster Than the National Average
paragraphs: Basilicata's self-service Metano price held at €2.199/L on November 20, unchanged from the previous day for the third straight tracked week. That's €0.0924/L, or 4.4%, above the €2.1066/L national self-service average — the region's largest premium of the four fuels today.

Metano has risen further than any other fuel tracked in Basilicata: up 57.1% since the week of July 20 (from €1.40/L — likely reflecting limited methane-station coverage early in the tracking window — to €2.199/L now), outpacing Italy's 40.9% national increase over the same period. Most of the regional jump came in a concentrated stretch between mid-October and early November (from €1.894/L to €2.199/L, +16.1%, versus a national rise of +10.2% over the same two weeks), after which both region and country plateaued — but the gap between them, close to nil in mid-October, had widened to today's 4.4% premium by late November.

network_section.heading: 238 of 268 Registered Stations Reporting Today
paragraphs: Basilicata had 268 registered fuel stations as of November 20, of which 238 reported prices that day — an 88.8% reporting rate. That trails Italy's national rate of 90.4% (21,678 of 23,971 stations), a gap of about 1.6 percentage points.

The region's station count has stayed remarkably stable across the tracked period, drifting only between 267 and 270 registered stations since late July, with the number reporting each day fluctuating in a narrow band of roughly 234 to 241. That suggests Basilicata's relatively small, well-established network reports with reasonable — if not quite national-leading — day-to-day consistency.

methodology_section.heading: Built, Not Maintained: How This Report Writes Itself
paragraphs: Everything in this report — today's regional pick, the weekly trend analysis, the station-network read, and the prose itself — is produced automatically each morning by an unattended pipeline built with Claude Code. A script pulls the day's price and registry data from Italy's MIMIT ministry feed (or a locally downloaded CSV when one is available), a second script deterministically rotates through Italy's 20 regions keyed to the calendar date, and an AI agent then composes the analysis you're reading from the real numbers those scripts produce, before another script renders it into this Word document and pushes the whole thing live.

Contrast that with how this kind of regional fuel-price tracking is normally done: someone manually downloads the day's spreadsheet, pastes the relevant rows into a workbook, recalculates a few averages by hand, and — if there's time — writes up a summary before moving on. Fuel Dashboard replaces that entire manual loop with code that runs itself daily, with no spreadsheet, no copy-paste, and no human in the chain between the raw data and the published report.

pull_quote: Basilicata's LPG price has barely moved in four months while Italy's climbed nearly 9% around it — the sharpest regional-vs-national divergence of any fuel tracked today.
caption:
Today's Fuel Dashboard spotlight is on Basilicata — and the standout number isn't gasoline or diesel, it's LPG. While Italy's national GPL price has climbed nearly 9% since late July, Basilicata's has actually gone nowhere, spending most of the autumn at its lowest tracked level before only a small recent uptick. Meanwhile Metano in the region has shot up 57% over the same stretch, outpacing the 41% national rise.

Fuel Dashboard is a fully automated project: a daily pipeline pulls Italy's official MIMIT price and station data, picks a new region to spotlight each day on a fixed rotation, computes the weekly trends, and writes up the analysis — all without a spreadsheet or a human in the loop. It's a live demonstration of what's possible when you build with AI tools like Claude Code instead of maintaining things by hand in Excel: the dashboard updates itself every morning, and so does this report.
